title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 209: The Deep-Ocean Mining Frontier
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 209 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Deep-Ocean Mining Frontier

Paragraph 1. Four thousand metres under the Pacific Ocean lies a flat, dark area called the Clarion-Clipperton Zone. The mud on the sea floor holds trillions of dark rocks about the size of a potato. These rocks, called nodules, formed slowly over millions of years. They are rich in useful metals like nickel and cobalt. Today, companies want to collect them because car makers need these metals to build batteries for millions of electric cars.

Paragraph 2. Mining companies say collecting rocks from the deep sea is cleaner than digging mines on land. On land, mining destroys rainforests and forces local people to leave their homes. In the deep sea, there are no trees to cut down and no towns nearby. However, ocean scientists strongly disagree. They found that freezing water and scarce food make deep-sea creatures grow and recover very slowly. Many animals even use the hard rocks as their only home on the soft mud floor.

Paragraph 3. Scientists have proof that ocean damage lasts a very long time. In 1989, researchers scraped a strip of seabed near Peru to test mining effects. Thirty years later, in 2019, robots checked the site and saw that the machine tracks still looked brand new, and animal numbers stayed eighty-five percent lower. Also, mining ships pump muddy water back into the middle ocean. This dirty cloud drifts for thousands of kilometres and may put harmful metals into fish like tuna.

Paragraph 4. Because the deep sea belongs to all countries, more than twenty-five nations want to pause ocean mining until science checks all risks. Instead of digging the seabed, many scientists say we should build new batteries without rare metals and recycle old electronics better.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...build batteries for millions of electric cars."

q5.text: Why do mining companies claim ocean mining is better than land mining?
options: A. Seabed rocks are much softer and easier to break.
B. There are no rainforests to cut down or local towns to move.
C. Ocean mining does not need any large ships or machines.
D. Sea water turns dangerous metals into safe salt.

steps: Đoạn 2: Dưới đáy biển sâu không có rừng rậm để chặt phá và không có làng mạc gần đó.

q6.text: Why do deep-sea animals recover slowly after their home is damaged?
options: A. Strong ocean waves push them away to shallow beaches.
B. Loud ship engines frighten them away from the area.
C. Bright underwater sunlight burns their soft skin.
D. Freezing water and scarce food make them grow very slowly.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...freezing water and scarce food make deep-sea creatures grow and recover very slowly."

q7.text: What happens when mining ships pump muddy water back into the ocean?
options: A. Dirty dust clouds drift far and may poison ocean fish.
B. The mud immediately turns into brand-new metal nodules.
C. Sunlight quickly cleans the muddy water within two hours.
D. The water cools down warm beaches along the coast.

steps: Đoạn 3: Đám mây bùn trôi dạt hàng nghìn km và có thể nhiễm kim loại độc vào cá.

q8.text: What solution do many scientists suggest instead of ocean mining?
options: A. Building heavier cars that run purely on petrol
B. Digging deeper mines inside tropical rainforests
C. Designing batteries without rare metals and improving recycling
D. Letting only rich island countries collect seabed rocks

steps: Đoạn 4: Chế tạo pin không cần kim loại hiếm và tái chế đồ điện tử cũ tốt hơn.
